item.title: Linux FUSE Readdir Cache Out-of-Bounds Write to Root LPE — CVE-2026-31694
item.description:
Metadata

Field Value

Last Updated 2026-06
Author / Researcher 0xCyberstan
CVE / Advisory CVE-2026-31694
Category binary
Severity High

Status Weaponized
Tags linux-kernel, fuse, oob-write, page-cache, lpe, groom, unprivileged, qemu-kvm
Related N/A

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System Linux kernel — fs/fuse/readdir.c (fuse_add_dirent_to_cache())
Versions Affected 6.15+ (the FUSE_NAME_MAX bump to PATH_MAX - 1 made the readdir path reachable); fixed by 51a8de6c50bf9
Language / Platform C, Linux kernel (FUSE), tested via QEMU/KVM guest
Authentication Required Local-only (ability to run a FUSE server as an unprivileged user, typical on many distros)
Network Access Required No

Summary

fuse_add_dirent_to_cache() is missing a bounds check when copying a FUSE server-supplied directory entry into the kernel’s readdir page-cache. A malicious (or attacker-controlled) FUSE server can return a dirent with namelen = 4095, which serializes to a 4120-byte record — 24 bytes larger than the single 4096-byte page-cache page the kernel copies it into, overflowing into the next physical page with fully server-controlled bytes. The included exploit uses a marker PoC to confirm the write primitive, then grooms the overflow so the 24 controlled bytes land on the page-cache copy of /etc/passwd, turning the root account passwordless for a full local privilege escalation.
